page: Amazon Web Services r7g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the custom ARM64 AWS Graviton3 processor family utilizing Neoverse-V1 cores. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with single-threaded core execution (no simultaneous multithreading). Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB of RAM, sustaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). Local instance storage is not included, requiring network-attached storage via Amazon EBS, while baseline network throughput is rated at 15 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs present.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate exceptional subsystem throughput in memory workloads. In PassMark memory testing, the instance achieves top-tier status within the top 10% (score of 3096.61), complemented by strong uncached large-block read (236.57 GB/sec) and write (105.19 GB/sec) bandwidths placing in the top 25%. Multi-core compute performance is robust, posting a strong Geekbench multi-core score of 17581.0 and PassMark database operations reaching 31222.38. However, single-core processing capabilities remain moderate, with stress-ng single-core (1532.48) and Geekbench single-core (1519.0) settling in the middle 50%. Large-model LLM generation exhibits clear performance ceilings due to lack of specialized matrix engines or discrete GPUs.

The absence of local disks necessitates dependency on network storage bandwidth for I/O-intensive workloads, though the dedicated 32 cores eliminate noisy neighbor core contention. Architecturally, the ARM64 platform offers superior computational and memory density per unit of infrastructure cost compared to legacy x86 alternatives, provided software stacks are compiled for ARM architectures.
The r7g.8xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, high-throughput key-value caches, enterprise data analytics, high-density web serving, and memory-bound ETL batch pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by 32 dedicated ARM64 AWS Graviton3 cores (Neoverse-V1) operating at 2.6 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 256.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, alongside 15 Gbps of baseline network throughput. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation reveals top-tier memory performance, achieving a PassMark memory score of 3096.61 (top 10%) alongside top-quartile uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 236 GB/sec for reads and 105 GB/sec for writes. Multi-core performance is strong with a Geekbench multi-core result of 17581.0, though single-thread metrics remain standard. Without local NVMe, persistent storage relies completely on remote volumes. Given its memory-dense profile and ARM power efficiency, r7g.8xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, distributed caching, memory-intensive data mining, and high-concurrency web services.
